speaker: N
text: Tap your foot on every green light. Only green.
picture: Frame 0, the LAB, bright and colourful: a big signal lamp fills the top of the frame; under it a young woman sits at one big button, finger ready, eyes wide. The lamp turns green on "green".

speaker: N
text: Go. Go. Go. Go. Go. Go. Go!
picture: The lamp flashes green on every "Go", with a bright beep, faster and faster; she presses each time, surer each time; the camera pushes in. On the last "Go!" the lamp is RED. Her hand comes down anyway. Half a second of silence.

speaker: N
text: Did you tap? She did.
picture: She freezes, hand on the button, staring up at the red lamp. A big red X.

speaker: N
text: In 1994, a railway lab in Japan set a trap like this. A hundred lights. Then, red.
picture: Wide: the lab, two rows of twelve people at button boards; a grinning researcher at a big switch; a board "1994"; a counter runs 98, 99, 100; one big RED floods the room.

speaker: N
text: Twelve people just watched. Five pressed anyway.
picture: The first row: five hands slam down, five red X's pop up, five faces freeze. Board: 5 OF 12.

speaker: N
text: Twelve others got one extra rule: point at the light and say it.
picture: The second row: twelve people point at their lamps and call, one after another, like a wave.

speaker: N
text: Not one pressed.
picture: RED: all twelve point at it, mouths open; twelve untouched buttons. Board: 0 OF 12.

speaker: N
text: After a hundred times, your hand stops waiting for your brain.
picture: A bored volunteer stares straight at the red lamp while his hand taps the button by itself.

speaker: N
text: That's how the cereal ends up in the fridge.
picture: A KITCHEN, morning: someone in pyjamas stands at the open fridge, staring at the cereal box sitting inside it.

speaker: N
text: Pointing and saying it makes your hand wait. Which is why Japan's train drivers point at their signals, and shout.
picture: The young woman from the start points at the red lamp and says it; her other hand stays off the button; a green tick. Cut on "Which": TODAY, a bright train glides into a sunny platform; in the cab the driver (cap, white gloves) snaps a crisp side-on point at a green signal; a kid at the front window copies him.

speaker: D
text: Signal clear!
picture: (same)

speaker: N
text: And where did it come from? The story goes, a steam-train driver's eyes had gone bad.
picture: Hard cut: a black STEAM ENGINE thunders through bright green fields under a blue sky, long white smoke. Cut on "The story": in the cab the driver leans forward to the little round window, peering hard; the signal ahead is a soft blur.

speaker: H
text: Signal clear!
picture: He turns and shouts across the cab.

speaker: N
text: So he shouted every signal to his coal man, who shouted back.
picture: The coal man, mid-shovel, fire glowing, leans out and looks at the signal post (arm lowered = clear),

speaker: C
text: Clear!
picture: and bellows it back with a huge grin.

speaker: N
text: His boss rode along, loved it, and made it a rule.
picture: The boss (dark suit, bowler hat) squeezed into the corner of the cab, delighted, writing in a notebook.

speaker: N
text: He never knew about the eyes.
picture: The driver nose to the glass, peering; behind him the boss beams and nods. Held.

speaker: N
text: New York copied the pointing: conductors must point at this board.
picture: A NEW YORK SUBWAY station: a conductor (navy uniform) leans from the middle window and points at a black-and-white striped board; only then do the doors open.

speaker: N
text: So two New Yorkers held up a sign: "Point here if you are dead sexy."
picture: A young man and a young woman hold up a big cardboard sign right under the board: POINT HERE IF YOU ARE DEAD SEXY.

speaker: N
text: And the conductors had to point.
picture: The conductor points at it, deadpan, then grins.

speaker: N
text: Now try again. This time, point, and say it.
picture: The big lamp and the young woman at the button, exactly as in frame 0; this time her arm is already up, pointing, mouth open. The film loops into line 1.
